title: Genome parametrizes a generative model; epigenesis inverts it

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Genome parametrizes a generative model; epigenesis inverts it

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Under the free-energy account of morphogenesis, genetic codes can be interpreted as parametrizing a generative model that predicts the signals each cell would sense in the target morphology, and epigenetic processes (signalling-dependent transcription) as the inversion of that model.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Friston K 2015, Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation › Abstract

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This novel perspective on the coordination of migration and differentiation of cells suggests an interpretation of genetic codes as parametrizing a generative model—predicting the signals sensed by cells in the target morphology—and epigenetic processes as the subsequent inversion of that model.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Friston K, Levin M, Sengupta B, Pezzulo G, “Knowing one's place: a free-energy approach to pattern regulation”, Journal of the Royal Society, Interface (2015), doi:10.1098/rsif.2014.1383; section “Abstract”. Scope: Morphogenesis in multicellular organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-place-02: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.23

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The model supplies a coherent interpretation, but the claim does not specify a distinct measurable consequence of calling genetic regulation a generative model and epigenesis its inversion. Existing morphogenesis data therefore cannot uniquely confirm or refute the interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: One could map genetic parameters to signal predictions and signalling-dependent transcription to model inversion, but no observation uniquely determines that this interpretation is preferable to ordinary regulatory-network descriptions.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Competing mechanistic descriptions predict the same observations.

The key terms are interpretive correspondences.

fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.15
analysis feasibility: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.2
operationalizability: 0.3
data existence: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a proposed reading of morphogenesis, phrased as an interpretation. Any coordinated signalling system can be redescribed as a generative model and its inversion, so existing expression or imaging data do not separate the reading from a non-cognitive account of the same molecular events.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The sentence offers an interpretation of genetic parameters as a generative model and of signalling-dependent transcription as inversion of that model. No measurement is specified that would accept this reading and reject an ordinary gene-regulatory description of the same signals.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Competing mechanistic descriptions fit the same signalling facts.

The mapping from genome and epigenesis onto a generative model is stipulated rather than tied to a distinct observable.
